title: Do You Still Need Figma if Canva Has AI Design Tools Now?
meta_title: Do You Still Need Figma if Canva Has AI Design Tools Now? | Aperture
summary: Canva's AI tools now handle most content design. But UI work, prototyping, and developer handoff still need Figma. Here's who actually needs which.

content:
Canva's AI tools can handle most everyday design work fast enough that you'd never miss Figma, if your work is mostly social graphics, presentations, or marketing materials. But Figma is still the only real choice for UI design, prototyping, and handing files to developers. The tools are growing toward each other, but they haven't met in the middle yet.

Key Takeaways

  • Canva's Magic Studio handles social media posts and marketing design well. Most content creators and small business owners don't need Figma.
  • Figma owns UI/UX workflows and developer handoff. No Canva equivalent exists for these jobs.
  • Indian freelance data shows Figma designers earning around 43% more than Canva-only designers, roughly ₹8L vs ₹5.6L annual median per Flexiple's 2026 data.
  • Canva bought the Affinity suite in 2024 and keeps adding professional tools, but core workflows still serve different jobs.
  • The honest split: content creators can skip Figma. Product and UI designers can't.

What Canva's AI Actually Does in 2026

Canva's Magic Studio bundles more than 25 AI tools, including text-to-image generation, background removal, automatic resizing across 100-plus format presets, and a Magic Design feature that generates a full layout from a single text prompt. It's fast, polished enough for most marketing work, and the free tier covers more than it used to.

The tool has come a long way. Canva acquired the Affinity suite in 2024, which added professional-grade vector editing and photo tools. The result is something that can handle tasks that once required separate desktop software.

For social posts, pitch decks, event flyers, or branded email headers, Canva doesn't just do the job, it does it faster than most people can open a blank Figma file. A decent template, a text prompt, maybe 10 minutes of editing. Done.

That shift has occured faster than most working designers expected. Three years ago, Canva was dismissed as a tool for making birthday cards. In 2026, large marketing agencies in India are running their full content output on it.

What Figma Still Does That Canva Can't Match

Figma handles real-time collaboration at a level Canva doesn't match. Its component system keeps changes synced across the whole file automatically. Prototypes feel like real apps, with smart transitions and clickable flows. And its Dev Mode hands developers pixel-accurate specs and downloadable assets, none of which Canva can replicate.

These things matter when you're building digital products. Figma's auto-layout keeps designs responsive as screen sizes change. Its variable system lets you manage multiple brand themes inside a single file. You can prototype an entire user flow and share it as a clickable demo with stakeholders, all without leaving the tool.

The developer handoff piece is the biggest gap. If you're working with a developer to build something real, a Canva file means screenshotting things and explaining spacing in Slack messages. Not a workflow.

The two tools are genuinely seperate even if they keep trying to grow into each other's space. Figma added Sites to build and publish websites. Canva added whiteboarding and more systematic design features. Neither has fully replaced what the other does best.

Canva vs Figma: Which Tool for Which Job

The real question isn't which is better. It's what you're actually doing. Here's the honest version:

Use CaseCanvaFigma
Social media graphicsStrongNot built for it
Presentations and decksStrongWorks, but slower
App and web UI designLimitedEssential
Developer handoffNot availableYes, via Dev Mode
Marketing collateralStrongPossible, not ideal
Clickable app prototypesBasicStrong

Most design jobs in India ask for both tools. But proficiency in Canva and Figma on a job listing usually means Canva for day-to-day content output and Figma for any work that goes to a developer. If your role doesn't touch developers at all, Canva alone might be enough.

Does the Figma Subscription Make Sense for Indian Designers?

Canva Pro runs around ₹4,999 a year. Figma's professional plan costs $15 per editor per month, roughly ₹1,250. That's a real gap. But Flexiple's mid-2026 hiring data shows Figma designers earning a median of ₹8 lakh a year versus ₹5.6 lakh for Canva-only designers, a 43% difference.

The math is straightforward if you're doing UI work. That extra ₹800-odd a month on Figma gets paid back by a single client project, sometimes in a day. Clients who need app screens or website mockups designed to hand off to developers expect Figma files, and they pay for the skill.

You'll recieve clear signal pretty quickly about which camp you're in. Clients asking for social campaigns and marketing materials will never need a Figma link. Clients who need something built will always ask for one.

Practical note: Figma's free tier is generous for solo designers. You can manage up to three active projects. That's enough for students and anyone learning the tool before they need to bill for it. Don't pay for the pro plan until the work actually demands it.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can Canva replace Figma for a UI designer?

Not really. Canva lacks real component systems, auto-layout, and developer handoff tools. You can mock up basic screens in it, but if a developer needs to build from your designs, they'll run into gaps fast. Figma remains the industry standard for UI work that goes into production.

Is Figma free for beginners?

Yes. Figma's free tier lets one editor work on up to three projects with unlimited viewers. That covers most students and early-career designers. You'd only need the paid plan once you're juggling multiple active client projects or working on a team where others need to edit your files.

Can I learn both Canva and Figma?

Yes, and it's worth doing. They take different skills. Canva's learning curve is low. Figma takes a few weeks to feel comfortable in, but free tutorials and official courses cover it well. Most working designers in India keep both open on an average day.

Which tool should Indian freelancers start with?

Start with Canva if your early clients are small businesses needing logos, social media graphics, or marketing materials. Add Figma once you're getting work that involves app screens or web design. Figma's free tier is enough while you're building skills and adding UI work to your portfolio.

Did Canva buy Figma?

No. Adobe tried to acquire Figma in 2022 for around $20 billion, but regulators blocked the deal in late 2023. Figma remains independent. Canva separately acquired the Affinity suite of creative tools in 2024 and has been adding professional capabilities since then.

What does AI change about this comparison?

Both tools have added substantial AI features. Canva's Magic Studio covers more content types with a broader toolset. Figma's AI design agent generates UI layouts from natural language prompts, which speeds up early-stage product design. AI makes both tools faster, but doesn't change what each is fundamentally built to do.

The Short Version

If you're making content, Canva is the right tool and Figma is probably overkill. If you're designing digital products that a developer will build, Figma is still the industry standard and Canva won't fill that gap. Most working designers in India use both, for different kinds of work on different days.
